# Angular facts

The scripts here answer "where is this used?" and "is this change finished?" from Angular's own tools. Ask them first;
search by text only for what the table below says no script sees.
- `<skill>` is the folder this file is in. `<ws>` is the workspace folder that doctor prints.
- Every command is `node <skill>/<script>.mjs <command> … --root <ws>`. `--all` lists every place. `--help` explains a script.
- Exit code 0: answered. 1: a wrong name, option, moment or folder, or a missing package: fix the call. 2: NOT finished
  (NOT DONE, NOT DECIDED, NOT FINISHED): do what the last lines say, run it again.
- A `!` line says what the script could not read: repeat it in your answer. A `→ next:` line is one command to paste, a
  suggestion, not the procedure: the steps below decide what you run. Never run a command twice for one question.

## Start: once per task
`node <skill>/doctor.mjs --root <the folder of the app, or the repository root>`

It prints `<ws>`, AngularJS yes or no, the cost of a language-service command, one line per script, and `READY` or `NOT READY`
with the fix. An `npm install --prefix …` line: run that exact line once (it installs into the skill folder, not the app), then
doctor again; if you may not install, use the scripts marked `ok` and say so. A script marked `NOT IN THIS COPY` or
`NOT USABLE HERE`: wherever a step names it, run the command its line gives instead.

## The question → the command
| The task asks | Run (each with `--root <ws>`) | It does not see |
|---|---|---|
| Who uses this component or directive? | `ng-facts usages <selector or Class>` | AngularJS templates (`ajs-facts usages`), elements created in code (`ls-facts refs <Class>`), the selector in style sheets (`git -C <ws> grep -n -w <selector> -- "*.css" "*.scss"`) |
| Who binds this input or output? | `ng-facts usages <Class>.<name>`, then `ls-facts refs <Class>.<name>` | names in text: `leftovers <Class>.<name> --before` |
| Who calls this method, reads or writes this property, uses this service member? | `ls-facts refs <Class>.<member>`, then `leftovers <Class>.<member> --before` | values typed `any`, code that does not compile |
| Where is this class, service or pipe used (templates, imports, injection, routes, types)? | `ls-facts refs <Class>` | the name in strings, files of no tsconfig |
| Who uses this function, constant (a store action or selector, a token), interface or enum? | no script: `git -C <ws> grep -n -w <name>`, and say it is a text search | |
| On which screens (routes, ui-router states) is this shown? | `ng-facts where <selector or Class>` (components and directives only) | routes and states built at run time |
| Is this component dead? Which ones are? | `ng-facts where <Class>` (all candidates: `ng-facts unrouted`), then `ls-facts refs <Class>` for each; with AngularJS also `ajs-facts usages <selector>` | a component picked by a string |
| Is this input or output dead? | `ls-facts refs <Class>.<name>`: its line "Text only" must say 0 and 0 | nothing more: both sources are in it |
| What breaks if I change or remove this? | procedure 2 | |
| Rename an input, output, method or property | procedure 3 | |
| Remove an input, an output or a component | procedure 4 | |
| Change a component's API in many templates | procedure 5 (`ng-facts migrate`) | TypeScript code, names in text |
| Move a class to another file | `<skill>/reference/move.md` | |
| What in AngularJS still uses this? What is left of AngularJS here? | procedure 6 (`ajs-facts`) | markup and names built at run time |
| Does the app compile? | `ls-facts check` (the build's project; `--all` lists every error place) | specs and stories (not in the build), every name that is only text |

## Which script when
- **ng-facts**: the compiler's template parser. Seconds. Works on code that does not compile. Knows templates, selectors,
  inputs, outputs, `extends`, routes and states. Does not see TypeScript code that reads a member through another object.
- **ls-facts**: the Angular Language Service, type-checked: inheritance, generics, services, TypeScript and templates together.
  Needs code that compiles. Slow on a big app (doctor says how slow): one command at a time, never in a loop or in parallel.
  `--warm` keeps the project loaded for 10 minutes: add it only if the user asks for it.
- **ajs-facts**: the AngularJS side of a hybrid app: registrations, AngularJS templates, states, downgraded Angular classes.
- **leftovers**: plain text: names in strings, styles, AngularJS templates, `.js` code, specs, stories, documents. Marks each
  place `CHANGE`, `leave` or `?`. Before a change pass `--before`; after it the OLD name. Its first word is the verdict.

## What no compiler sees, and what no script sees
- A name that is only text stays wrong while the compiler is green: `setInput("name")`, `inputs: ["name"]`, `args: { name: … }`,
  `some-tag[name]` in a style sheet, `my-name="…"` in an AngularJS template, `service.name()` in a `.js` file.
  **A green compiler is not proof. Only `leftovers … --final` printing `FINISHED` is.**
- No script sees: markup and names built at run time, a component picked by a string, values typed `any`, code outside this workspace.

## Rules for every task
1. Do not cut script output with `head` or `tail`. The first line is the verdict and the counts; read on for the places.
2. Do not replace a word everywhere (`sed`, find-and-replace in files). Other things share the name. Edit only a place a script listed.
3. Do not stop at a green compiler. Do not skip a gate. A gate is a command that must exit 0 before you go on.
4. Every number in your answer is copied from a script's output. Say which script printed it.

## Procedures

**1. Answer a usage question** (nothing is edited)
1. Run the command from the table. Gate: exit 0.
2. An input, an output or a component: the second source too (`ls-facts refs …` after `ng-facts usages …`). Numbers differ:
   say both and why (ng-facts counts story and test templates, ls-facts TypeScript code); list what you cannot explain.
3. A member: `leftovers <Class>.<name> --before`. A component in an app with AngularJS: `ajs-facts usages <selector>`. Gate: exit 0.
4. Answer: the counts per group, `file:line` of the places asked about, which script said what, every `!` line.

**2. Before changing or removing a member: impact** (nothing is edited)
1. `ls-facts refs <Class>.<member>`: everything the type checker ties to the member, and one line "Text only" with the places
   only text shows. Gate: exit 0. Exit 1 "no member": the name is wrong; fix it now.
2. `leftovers <Class>.<member> --before`: those text places, each `file:line` (strings, styles, AngularJS templates, `.js`
   code, stories, tests). An input or an output: also `ng-facts usages <Class>.<member>` (it reads story templates). Gate: exit 0.
3. A component or a directive: `ng-facts where <Class>` (screens to test). A service: who injects it is `ls-facts refs <Class>`.
4. Report: type-checked references per group, text-only places (`CHANGE` and `?`, each `file:line`), screens.

**3. Rename a member** — every step: `<skill>/reference/rename.md`
1. Procedure 2. Keep its counts.
2. Plan: `ls-facts rename <Class>.<old> <new>`. Read every `!` line. Gate: exit 0.
3. Apply: the same command with `--write`. Its first line says "written". `--write` is never the last step: exit 2 and
   `NOT DONE` is the usual answer here (text places the service cannot see, or a place that needs your decision): go to step 4.
   No language service: `ng-facts rename-input <Class>.<old> <new> --write` (inputs and outputs only), then `ng-facts check --all`.
4. `leftovers <Class>.<old>`. Edit each `CHANGE` place by hand: that line, that name, nothing else. A `?` place, and a place in
   a `*.stories.ts` or `*.spec.ts` file: read `<skill>/reference/deciding.md` first (there one place can mean two edits).
   Run it again. `NOT DONE`: go on with the list. `NOT DECIDED`: decide each `?`; one you leave on purpose goes into
   `--decided <file:line>`. Gate: it prints `DONE` and exits 0.
5. Last gate: `leftovers <Class>.<old> --final` (same `--decided`); it runs the compiler too. Gate: `FINISHED`, exit 0. An error
   names a place: fix it, run it again. Each spec or story you edited: `git -C <ws> diff -- <file>`, "reviewed by diff, not compiled".

**4. Remove an input, an output or a component** — every step: `<skill>/reference/remove.md`
1. Procedure 2 (a component: the "dead" row of the table). Something still uses it: stop and report the uses; if the task says
   to remove them too, remove each listed use first. 2. Remove the declaration. 3. `leftovers <Class>.<name>` until `DONE`,
   exit 0. 4. `leftovers <Class>.<name> --final`: `FINISHED`, exit 0. 5. Report table.

**5. Change a component's API with a spec** — every step: `<skill>/reference/migrate.md`
1. `ng-facts migrate --help` prints the spec format; write the spec to a file. 2. Dry run: `ng-facts migrate <spec.json>`; read
   every `needs a decision` line. 3. The same with `--write`. Gate: it prints `nothing left to migrate`; exit 2 means decisions
   are left: make them by hand. 4. For each renamed or removed input: `leftovers <Class>.<old>` until `DONE`.
5. `leftovers <Class>.<old> --final`: `FINISHED`, exit 0 (no input renamed: `ls-facts check`, `0 errors`). 6. Report table.

**6. AngularJS questions** (nothing is edited) — every step: `<skill>/reference/angularjs.md`
1. `ajs-facts summary`: counts per kind. `ajs-facts list <components|directives|filters|services|downgrades|wrappers|states>`;
   add `--unused` for what nothing uses, `--under <folder>` for what one feature folder registers.
2. One thing: `ajs-facts show <name>` (its card) and `ajs-facts usages <name>` (every use, `file:line`). Gate: exit 0.
3. An Angular input in an AngularJS template (kebab-case): `ajs-facts usages <name>.<input>`. A service method called from
   AngularJS code: `leftovers <Class>.<method> --before` (group "AngularJS code in .js files").

## The report: after every change, this table
| | count | where |
|---|---|---|
| changed by a script | n | the command and the groups it printed |
| changed by hand | n | each `file:line` |
| left on purpose | n | each `file:line` (your `--decided` places) and what it is instead |
| not decided | n | each `file:line` and what you saw: the user decides |
| gates | | `leftovers --final`: FINISHED or NOT FINISHED · `git diff --stat`: files changed |

## When something goes wrong
- `@angular/language-service` is not installed: run the `npm install --prefix …` line the script prints, once. Until then
  use ng-facts, leftovers and `ls-facts check` (check needs no language service), and say so in the report.
- The code does not compile: ls-facts returns fewer references. Use ng-facts, fix what `ls-facts check` lists, then ask ls-facts.
- "lists no source files" or "name the project": add `--project <tsconfig>` with a config doctor listed. Slow: wait, as doctor said.
- `!` "templates with parse errors" or "not read at all": the answer does not cover those files. Read the ones your task is about; name the others.
- "no class", "no member", "several classes answer to": copy the name from its source file; two classes share it: `<file>#<Class>`.
  leftovers "still declares … --before" or "declares no member": the wrong name for the moment: fix the call as the line says.

# Rename a member (input, output, method, property): every step

`<skill>` is the skill folder, `<ws>` the workspace folder doctor printed, `<Class>.<old>` the member, `<new>` the new name.
Do the steps in order. A step is finished when its gate holds. Do not go on before that.

## 0. Before

1. `node <skill>/doctor.mjs --root <ws>` if you have not run it in this task. Gate: `READY`, or you know which scripts are `ok`.
2. `git -C <ws> status --short`. Write down the files that are already changed: they are not yours. (Doctor says "git: no": skip.)

## 1. Impact (nothing is edited)

1. `node <skill>/ls-facts.mjs refs <Class>.<old> --root <ws>`
2. `node <skill>/leftovers.mjs <Class>.<old> --root <ws> --before`

Keep the number of references from 1 and the number of `CHANGE` and `?` places from 2.
Gate: both exit 0. Exit 1 with "no class", "no member" or "declares no member": the name is wrong. Fix the name. Do not go on with a guess.

## 2. Plan

`node <skill>/ls-facts.mjs rename <Class>.<old> <new> --root <ws>`

It prints the edits per group and writes nothing. Read every line that starts with `!`:

| The `!` line says | What you do |
|---|---|
| "added by the template parser", with places | they are part of the rename; after step 3 open each listed place and see that it has the new name |
| "with syntax errors" | after step 3 open that template; a binding of `<Class>` that still has the old name: change it by hand |
| "in a template built from an expression … look by hand" | open each listed place; it is this member: change the name by hand after step 3 |
| "under a derived name … NOT renamed, fix by hand" | after step 3 change each listed place by hand (step 3 also ends with `NOT DONE` and exit 2 for these) |
| "inherits `<old>` from `<Base>`" | the rename changes the member of `<Base>`, so every class that extends `<Base>` changes too. The task meant only `<Class>`: stop and ask |
| "uses the alias … which stays" | nothing: templates bind the alias, and the alias does not change |
| "(`<old>`Change) … becomes (`<new>`Change)" | nothing: the event of a `model()` is renamed with it |
| "edited files are outside `<tsconfig>`, the project check compiles (specs, stories): check cannot vouch for them" | `check` compiles the build only: in step 5 read the diff of each of those files yourself and write "reviewed by diff, not compiled" in the report |
| "outside `<tsconfig>` hold the name … drop --project" | run the command again without `--project` |
| "no tsconfig could load … read by hand" | open the listed files; `leftovers` in step 4 judges them too |
| "switched on in memory", "the service returned N entries for M places", "findRenameLocations returned … built from the references" | nothing: this is how the answer was made complete |
| "also feed `<Other>`.`<old>` on the same element" | one attribute feeds two directives. After step 3 decide each listed place: keep the old name there too (add an attribute) or accept that `<Other>` loses it; ask when unsure. Name each place in the report |
| "the selector … is the input's own name and is NOT renamed" | the directive is matched by `[<old>]`. Ask the user whether the selector changes too; leftovers marks it `?` |

Exit 1 "is also declared outside the workspace's own sources": the member implements or overrides a library member (a lifecycle
hook, `PipeTransform.transform`). It cannot be renamed alone. Stop and tell the user.

Gate: exit 0, and the number of edits is close to the number of references from step 1 (the same, or lower by the places a
`!` line explains). Exit 1 "already has a member": the new name is taken. Stop and ask the user for another name.

## 3. Apply

`node <skill>/ls-facts.mjs rename <Class>.<old> <new> --root <ws> --write`

The first line says "written". Then it runs `leftovers` itself and says what is left: `--write` is never the last step.
- `NOT DONE: N places in text still carry …` and exit 2: the usual case. Go to step 4; `leftovers` lists them.
- `NOT DONE: … under a derived name` or `… need your decision`: change or decide each listed place by hand, then go to step 4.
- Exit 0 and "leftovers finds no place": go to step 5.
Gate: the first line says "written" (exit 0 or 2). Exit 1: nothing was written; read the line.

**No language service** (doctor said `ls-facts.mjs CANNOT RUN` and you may not install it, or `NOT IN THIS COPY`), for an
input or an output. This replaces steps 2 and 3:
1. `node <skill>/ng-facts.mjs rename-input <Class>.<old> <new> --root <ws>`, read the counts, then the same with `--write`
   (it ends with exit 2 and `NOT DONE`: the compiler and leftovers still have to speak).
   It renames the declaration, the reads in the class and in its own template, and every binding, also on components that
   extend `<Class>`. It does not see TypeScript code that reads the member through another object.
2. `node <skill>/ls-facts.mjs check --root <ws> --all` (`ls-facts.mjs` is not in this copy: `node <skill>/ng-facts.mjs check
   --root <ws> --all`, the same compiler). Each `file:line:column` it lists under "Property '`<old>`' does not exist" is such
   a read: change the name at that place, nothing else. Run it again (a line with two reads shows the second one only now),
   until it prints `0 errors`. Then go on with step 4: the compiler has not seen the strings and the styles.
A method or a property without the language service: change the declaration by hand, then fix every error `check` prints, the same way.

## 4. Leftovers: the places no compiler checks

`node <skill>/leftovers.mjs <Class>.<old> --root <ws>`

- `CHANGE` places: edit each one by hand: the name on that line, nothing else. A line listed twice holds two places: change both.
- A `CHANGE` place in a `*.stories.ts` or `*.spec.ts` file: first read "Stories and tests" in `<skill>/reference/deciding.md`.
  A story template line `[old]="old"` is listed twice: change both sides (`[new]="new"`).
- `?` places: decide each one with `<skill>/reference/deciding.md`. Changed: it disappears. Left on purpose: add it to the
  command as `--decided <file:line>` (several: `--decided a.ts:3,b.html:7`); the script then lists it as decided.
- `leave` counts: nothing to do. They are other things with the same name.
- "+N more": run it with `--all` to see every place.

Run the same command again after your edits.
Gate: it prints `DONE` and exits 0. `NOT DONE` and exit 2: `CHANGE` places are left. `NOT DECIDED` and exit 2: a `?` is open.
Go on with them. Do not skip to step 5.

## 5. The last gate: text and compiler together

`node <skill>/leftovers.mjs <Class>.<old> --root <ws> --final` (with the same `--decided` as in step 4)

It runs step 4 again and then the compiler (`check`). Gate: `FINISHED`, exit 0. It takes as long as doctor said for `check`.
Run it once, wait for it, never two at once. `NOT FINISHED`: the compiler lists its places as `file:line:column` (add `--all`
for every place): fix each place, run it again.
An error that does not name `<old>` or `<new>`, in a file that `git -C <ws> diff --stat` does not list, was there before
your change: do not fix it. Put it in the report as "error not from this change" with its `file:line`.

`check` compiles the build's project. Spec and story files are not in it, and no gate of this procedure compiles them.
For each spec or story file that step 3 named ("check cannot vouch for them") or that you edited in step 4:
`git -C <ws> diff -- <file>`. Every changed line must change the name and nothing else. Write in the report
"specs and stories: reviewed by diff, not compiled", with the files.
Only when the user asks for the tests to be compiled: `node <skill>/ls-facts.mjs check --root <ws> --project <the test
tsconfig doctor named>`. On a big app it can take many minutes, and it often lists errors that were there before (components
that exist only inside a test). Report only the errors that name `<old>` or `<new>`; never fix the others.

## 6. Review and report

1. `git -C <ws> diff --stat`. Every file in it comes from step 3 or step 4. A file you cannot explain: read its diff; undo
   what the task did not ask for.
2. Write the report table from SKILL.md: changed by a script (the number of edits step 3 printed, per group), changed by hand
   (each `file:line`), left on purpose (each `--decided` place and what it is), not decided, and the gate
   (`leftovers --final`: FINISHED).

## What a rename does not do

- It does not rename the file, the class or the selector.
- It does not change prose in documents. `leftovers` lists the documents that name the member: decide with the user.
- In an AngularJS template the name is written in kebab-case (`[old-name]`, `(old-name)`). Only `leftovers` lists those.
----
# Whose name is this? How to decide a place by hand

Use this for every line `leftovers` marks `?`, and before every edit you make by hand.
`<Class>.<name>` is the member the task is about.

## The forms a member name takes

| Where | How the name is written | Who checks it |
|---|---|---|
| Angular template, bound | `[name]="…"`, `[(name)]="…"`; an output: `(name)="…"`; a `model()`: also `(nameChange)="…"` | compiler, ng-facts, ls-facts |
| Angular template, plain attribute | `<some-tag name>` or `<some-tag name="text">` | ng-facts, ls-facts; the compiler does NOT |
| AngularJS template (a `.html` file Angular does not compile) | kebab-case: `[my-name]="…"`, `my-name="…"`, `(my-name)="…"`, `bind-my-name`, `on-my-name` | only leftovers |
| TypeScript code | `thing.name`, `thing.name()`, `this.name.set(…)` | compiler, ls-facts |
| A string in code | `setInput("name", …)`, `inputs: ["name"]`, `inputs: ["name: alias"]` in `hostDirectives`, `@HostBinding("attr.name")`, `By.css("some-tag[name]")` | only leftovers |
| A story or a test | `args: { name: … }`, `componentInputs: { name: … }`, `componentProperties`, `props` | only leftovers |
| A style sheet, or `styles:` of a component | `some-tag[name]`, `[name]`, `.some-class[name]` | only leftovers |
| Documentation | the name in prose or in a code sample | nobody: decide with the user |

## The decision, step by step

1. Find what the place talks about: the element (the tag the attribute sits on, or the tag before `[name]` in a style
   selector) or the class (the component a test creates, the `component:` of a story, the `directive:` of a host directive).
2. An element: ask which class owns the tag. `node <skill>/ng-facts.mjs usages <tag> --root <ws>` prints the class and its
   file in the first line. "no component or directive" and exit 1: the tag is not an Angular component of this project.
3. The class is `<Class>`, or a class that extends it (`leftovers` prints the family in its second line; the other scripts
   print "extends `<Class>`"): it is the member. **Change it.**
4. The class is something else, or the tag is a plain HTML element: it only shares the name. **Leave it** and put it in the
   report under "left on purpose" with the class you found.
5. You cannot find the element or the class (a string built at run time, prose, a tag nobody declares): do not guess.
   Leave it and put it in the report under "not decided" with the line you saw.

## How to edit by hand

- Change the name on that line only. Keep the form: `[old]` becomes `[new]`, `old-name` becomes `new-name` in an AngularJS
  template, `"old"` becomes `"new"` in a string.
- One place, one edit. Never run a replace over a file or a folder.
- After the edits run the same `leftovers` command again. A `?` you leave on purpose (step 4) or cannot decide (step 5) goes
  into the command as `--decided <file:line>` and into the report. It is finished when it prints `DONE` and exits 0;
  `NOT DECIDED` means a `?` is still open.

## Cases that fool a reader

- **Alias.** `input({ alias: "shown" })` or `@Input("shown")`: templates bind `shown`, code reads the member name.
  Renaming the member does not change templates while the alias stays; `ls-facts rename` says so in a `!` line.
- **Two-way.** A `model()` named `value` is bound as `[(value)]`, `[value]` and `(valueChange)`. A rename changes all three forms.
- **Declared again in a subclass.** A class that extends `<Class>` and declares the same name again has a member of its own.
  Do not decide alone whether it is part of the task: put it under "not decided".
- **Two owners on one element.** `<some-tag [name]>` where a directive on the same element also has an input `name`: the one
  attribute feeds both. Changing it for one breaks the other: put it under "not decided".
- **A word inside a longer word.** `name-size`, `nameChange`, `--name`, `data-name` are other names. Leave them, except
  `(nameChange)` of a `model()` (the row above).
- **The same line twice.** A line that `leftovers` lists twice holds the name twice (two selectors, two attributes): two places.

## Stories and tests: two cases where one place means two edits

No compiler reads a template that is a string in a story or a test, so nothing warns you here.

- **A story template reads the keys of `args`.** In a `*.stories.ts` file the template string is fed from `args`
  (`args: { name: … }`, `argTypes: { name: … }`). The type-checked rename renames those keys (its group "set as a key of an
  object literal", in spec/stories files). Then in the template string of that file the same word on the RIGHT side of a
  binding is that key and must follow: `[old]="old"` becomes `[new]="new"`, both sides. `leftovers` lists such a line
  twice: once for the left side, once for the right side ("the right side of … reads …"). The right side is `?` while the
  file still has a key `old` (it follows that key) and `CHANGE` once the key is renamed.
- **A test stub stands in for the component.** A stub class in a spec with the same selector has its own copy of the member;
  `leftovers` marks it `CHANGE` ("stands in for … in a test"). After you rename it, the spec's own code that reads the stub
  (`stub.old()`, `setInput("old", …)` on the stub) must follow too.

After editing such a file by hand, run `git -C <ws> grep -n -w "<old>" -- <that file>` (doctor said "git: no":
`grep -n -w "<old>" <that file>`). Every line it still prints must be something you can name (another component's
attribute, a comment, a field of the test's own host component). Put those under "left on purpose".
`check` compiles the build only: a spec or a story is in no gate. Its diff (`git -C <ws> diff -- <that file>`) is the review;
write "reviewed by diff, not compiled" in the report.

----
# Whose name is this? How to decide a place by hand

Use this for every line `leftovers` marks `?`, and before every edit you make by hand.
`<Class>.<name>` is the member the task is about.

## The forms a member name takes

| Where | How the name is written | Who checks it |
|---|---|---|
| Angular template, bound | `[name]="…"`, `[(name)]="…"`; an output: `(name)="…"`; a `model()`: also `(nameChange)="…"` | compiler, ng-facts, ls-facts |
| Angular template, plain attribute | `<some-tag name>` or `<some-tag name="text">` | ng-facts, ls-facts; the compiler does NOT |
| AngularJS template (a `.html` file Angular does not compile) | kebab-case: `[my-name]="…"`, `my-name="…"`, `(my-name)="…"`, `bind-my-name`, `on-my-name` | only leftovers |
| TypeScript code | `thing.name`, `thing.name()`, `this.name.set(…)` | compiler, ls-facts |
| A string in code | `setInput("name", …)`, `inputs: ["name"]`, `inputs: ["name: alias"]` in `hostDirectives`, `@HostBinding("attr.name")`, `By.css("some-tag[name]")` | only leftovers |
| A story or a test | `args: { name: … }`, `componentInputs: { name: … }`, `componentProperties`, `props` | only leftovers |
| A style sheet, or `styles:` of a component | `some-tag[name]`, `[name]`, `.some-class[name]` | only leftovers |
| Documentation | the name in prose or in a code sample | nobody: decide with the user |

## The decision, step by step

1. Find what the place talks about: the element (the tag the attribute sits on, or the tag before `[name]` in a style
   selector) or the class (the component a test creates, the `component:` of a story, the `directive:` of a host directive).
2. An element: ask which class owns the tag. `node <skill>/ng-facts.mjs usages <tag> --root <ws>` prints the class and its
   file in the first line. "no component or directive" and exit 1: the tag is not an Angular component of this project.
3. The class is `<Class>`, or a class that extends it (`leftovers` prints the family in its second line; the other scripts
   print "extends `<Class>`"): it is the member. **Change it.**
4. The class is something else, or the tag is a plain HTML element: it only shares the name. **Leave it** and put it in the
   report under "left on purpose" with the class you found.
5. You cannot find the element or the class (a string built at run time, prose, a tag nobody declares): do not guess.
   Leave it and put it in the report under "not decided" with the line you saw.

## How to edit by hand

- Change the name on that line only. Keep the form: `[old]` becomes `[new]`, `old-name` becomes `new-name` in an AngularJS
  template, `"old"` becomes `"new"` in a string.
- One place, one edit. Never run a replace over a file or a folder.
- After the edits run the same `leftovers` command again. A `?` you leave on purpose (step 4) or cannot decide (step 5) goes
  into the command as `--decided <file:line>` and into the report. It is finished when it prints `DONE` and exits 0;
  `NOT DECIDED` means a `?` is still open.

## Cases that fool a reader

- **Alias.** `input({ alias: "shown" })` or `@Input("shown")`: templates bind `shown`, code reads the member name.
  Renaming the member does not change templates while the alias stays; `ls-facts rename` says so in a `!` line.
- **Two-way.** A `model()` named `value` is bound as `[(value)]`, `[value]` and `(valueChange)`. A rename changes all three forms.
- **Declared again in a subclass.** A class that extends `<Class>` and declares the same name again has a member of its own.
  Do not decide alone whether it is part of the task: put it under "not decided".
- **Two owners on one element.** `<some-tag [name]>` where a directive on the same element also has an input `name`: the one
  attribute feeds both. Changing it for one breaks the other: put it under "not decided".
- **A word inside a longer word.** `name-size`, `nameChange`, `--name`, `data-name` are other names. Leave them, except
  `(nameChange)` of a `model()` (the row above).
- **The same line twice.** A line that `leftovers` lists twice holds the name twice (two selectors, two attributes): two places.

## Stories and tests: two cases where one place means two edits

No compiler reads a template that is a string in a story or a test, so nothing warns you here.

- **A story template reads the keys of `args`.** In a `*.stories.ts` file the template string is fed from `args`
  (`args: { name: … }`, `argTypes: { name: … }`). The type-checked rename renames those keys (its group "set as a key of an
  object literal", in spec/stories files). Then in the template string of that file the same word on the RIGHT side of a
  binding is that key and must follow: `[old]="old"` becomes `[new]="new"`, both sides. `leftovers` lists such a line
  twice: once for the left side, once for the right side ("the right side of … reads …"). The right side is `?` while the
  file still has a key `old` (it follows that key) and `CHANGE` once the key is renamed.
- **A test stub stands in for the component.** A stub class in a spec with the same selector has its own copy of the member;
  `leftovers` marks it `CHANGE` ("stands in for … in a test"). After you rename it, the spec's own code that reads the stub
  (`stub.old()`, `setInput("old", …)` on the stub) must follow too.

After editing such a file by hand, run `git -C <ws> grep -n -w "<old>" -- <that file>` (doctor said "git: no":
`grep -n -w "<old>" <that file>`). Every line it still prints must be something you can name (another component's
attribute, a comment, a field of the test's own host component). Put those under "left on purpose".
`check` compiles the build only: a spec or a story is in no gate. Its diff (`git -C <ws> diff -- <that file>`) is the review;
write "reviewed by diff, not compiled" in the report.
